title: Endpoint buyer risk matrix + demo hooks for managed AI buyers
content:
Purpose: quick internal playbook to map buyer risks for managed AI/endpoint customers (SaaS + mid-market + platform teams) and turn those risks into demo hooks and battle-tested counters vs AWS/GCP/Azure managed endpoints.

Context / why this doc exists:
- We keep hearing the same buyer questions when the field goes head-to-head with hyperscaler managed endpoints: 'cost unpredictability', 'vendor lock', 'opacity into latency and throttling', 'data residency', 'SLA guarantees', 'multi-region failover', and 'operational ownership for production-scale workloads'.
- This doc is deliberately tactical: short risk matrix, prioritized demo hooks for each buyer persona, 1–2 lines of rebuttal language, and measurable demo artifacts (metrics to show, prompts to run).

Audience:
- Solutions Engineers, AE pre-sales, Growth PMs who build trial experiences, and Content for battle cards.

High-level positioning summary (one-liner):
- Redwood reduces operational risk while improving unit economics: predictable reserved capacity, transparent latency/cost telemetry, and fallbacks that keep apps live when hyperscalers throttle or reallocate capacity.

Buyer personas and demo framing:
1) Product/Feature PM (SaaS app) - cares about UX latency, cost/unit, rollout safety. Demo hook: show 95th/99th latency pre/post batching and cache for a customer prompt set.
2) Platform/Infra (internal platform team) - cares about isolation, network control, observability, and lock-in. Demo hook: show private deployment (VPC) config + KMS integration and quick rollback to pinned model version.
3) Security/Compliance - cares about data residency, audit logs, and certified KMS/HSM. Demo hook: show Private deployment audit trail and key rotation workflow.
4) Finance/Procurement - cares about predictable spend and reserved capacity commitments. Demo hook: run cost-per-1k-tokens calc with and without dedicated pools during peak QPS.

Buyer risk matrix (prioritized):
- Columns: risk / buyer types impacted / root cause / Redwood demo hook / quick rebuttal phrase
1) Cost surprise / PM, Finance / Spiky load + pay-as-you-go models / Show Dedicated vs hosted cost delta with simple traffic pattern sim / "Reserved capacity flattens unit cost; we show you the numbers during the POC."
2) Latency spikes / PM, Platform / Multi-tenant noisy neighbors, autoscaler lag / Live 95/99 latency traces with and without autoscaler headroom + fallback to lighter quantized model / "Our routing and fallback keep tail latency predictable even when clouds backfill GPUs."
3) Data/control / Platform, Security / Shared control planes and opaque routing / Demo private control plane + KMS + VPC endpoints + retention settings / "You own keys and logs; our control plane accepts your network controls."
4) Resilience / PM, SRE / Region outages, capacity preemption / Show canary rollover + cross-region fallback in console traces / "Automatic model fallback and region routing keeps the app available."
5) Quality drift / PM, Research / Model upgrades that change outputs / Show rollout canary with evals, rollback, and prompts comparison; integrate Redwood Optimize recommendations / "Rollouts are small, measured, and reversible; we tie regressions to your prompt set."

Competitive callouts (direct vs AWS/GCP/Azure managed endpoints) - tactical language for SEs:
- AWS SageMaker-style managed endpoints:
  - Strengths: deep infra integration with broader AWS services, familiar IAM, marketplace placement.
  - Weaknesses/Buyer pain: opaque autoscaling behavior, billing fragmentation, limited fallback between instance types/models.
  - Redwood counters/demo: emphasize Dedicated pools for steady-state QPS, show cost visibility (token-level) and cross-model fallback policy. Demo: simulate instance preemption and show automatic fallback to quantized variant with no 503s.
- GCP Vertex AI-style endpoints:
  - Strengths: strong MLOps integrations, Vertex Viz tools, global cloud network.
  - Weaknesses/Buyer pain: limited on-prem/VPC private control plane options, SLA/throughput ties to provisioned instances.
  - Redwood counters/demo: highlight Private deployment and VPC-managed control plane; show network policy enforcement and audit trail. Demo: live console showing KMS key rotation and region-specific routing.
- Azure ML/Managed Endpoints:
  - Strengths: enterprise sales motion, M365 integration, Azure AD.
  - Weaknesses/Buyer pain: higher latency variability in some regions, complex cost model, and can be slow for rapid multi-model rollouts.
  - Redwood counters/demo: show rapid canary rollouts and per-route token cost breakdowns; demonstrate A/B rollout and instant rollback with traceable customer examples.

Demo artifacts and measurable signals to show (minimal set):
- 90/95/99 latency times for a representative prompt set (baseline vs Redwood tuning).
- Cost per 1k tokens: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Fallback quantized model.
- Console screenshot/video: per-route token breakdown, rollout history, and the single-trace view that maps request->model->latency->cost.
- Failure scenario: a synthetic capacity preemption (throttle) that triggers our fallback and shows zero customer-facing errors.
- Eval metrics: show a small regression check for rollout (precision/recall or BLEU/embedding similarity) on a curated prompt set we get from the prospect.

Demo scripts (short templates):
- PM demo script: "We're going to run your top 10 prompts through the hosted endpoint then switch to Dedicated (pinned) with caching and measure tail latency and cost. Watch the 99th latency and tokens/second. Here are the numbers you can expect at 10k QPS vs your current setup."
- Infra demo script: "We'll show the private control plane UI: KMS key binding, per-route access controls, and then simulate a regional failover. You can see logs/audit trail for every request."

Common objections + suggested responses:
- Objection: 'We use AWS/GCP already — don't want to rip out infra.'
  - Response: "Redwood interops — we can run in your VPC or provide a dedicated pool integrated with your cloud billing. You can incrementally adopt Dedicated for critical paths while leaving lower-volume traffic on your current provider."
- Objection: 'What about cost?'
  - Response: "Let's model it. We typically see x%-y% unit cost reduction for predictable workloads using reserved capacity; for spiky workloads caching and continuous batching reduce cost per token significantly. We'll run a short traffic sim during the POC and show exact numbers."
- Objection: 'How do we avoid regressions on model upgrades?'
  - Response: "We tie rollouts to your prompt set and continuous eval; any statistically significant regression blocks the rollout and triggers an automatic rollback policy. We'll demonstrate with your own test prompts."

Open questions / TODOs (for SEs & demo owners):
- Collect 10 canonical prompts from each active AE opportunity (ask for a small prompt set in discovery). TODO: add prompt collection template to the POC kickoff checklist. (Owner: Priya)
- Build a short failing-scenario harness that simulates instance preemption for demo labs. (Owner: Marco, JIRA-ENG-9123)
- Create a short 90-second animated clip that highlights "fallback to compatible model variant" for use on calls and deck. (Owner: Marketing)

Appendix - quick scripts/commands to run during POC (notes to SEs):
- Use our sample traffic driver (github link above) with the customer's prompts at 1k/5k/10k QPS to capture curves.
- Capture token-level billing for 30 minutes during peak run and export CSV to show finance.
- Always include a rollback demo: start canary at 10% then force a regression and hit rollback and show logs.

Notes to self / rough fragments (work-in-progress):
- Think about a 1-page PDF "Hyperscaler comparison at a glance" that the AE can use in first call. Should focus on five signals (cost, latency, availability, control, compliance).
- Add a short case study snippet about a customer who moved critical inference to Dedicated and avoided a major outage during a cloud capacity shortage. Need to get PO clearance to share details.

End.
